mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in CPIAUCSL above 3% over two consecutive quarters signals persistent inflation, which prompts the Federal Reserve to raise interest rates, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or inflation above 3% persists without subsequent rate hikes.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in GDPC1 for three consecutive quarters indicates weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 falls for three consecutive quarters
failure_condition: GDPC1 declines for three quarters but S&P 500 posts positive 60-day returns in more than 70% of such instances.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in UNRATE above 6% for two consecutive months signals a tight labor market, which increases wage pressure and input costs, ultimately reducing profit margins and leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: UNRATE exceeds 6% for two months but S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in INDPRO above its 12-month moving average for six consecutive months signals robust industrial production growth, which boosts corporate earnings and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO > 12-month moving average for six consecutive months
failure_condition: INDPRO remains above its 12-month moving average for six months but S&P 500 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of such periods.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in FEDFUNDS and a decline in RSAFS over two months signals a tightening monetary policy stance, which raises discount rates and reduces equity valuations, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises while RSAFS falls over two months
failure_condition: FEDFUNDS rises and RSAFS falls for two months but S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of such episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A coordinated rise in GDPC1 and HOUST over three months signals strengthening housing demand and broader economic activity, which boosts consumer spending and corporate profits, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 and HOUST both rise for three consecutive months
failure_condition: GDPC1 and HOUST rise for three months but S&P 500 60-day returns are negative in more than 60% of such periods.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent fall in PAYEMS below its 12-month moving average for four consecutive months signals weakening labor market conditions, which depresses consumer spending and corporate earnings, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS < 12-month moving average for four consecutive months
failure_condition: PAYEMS remains below its 12-month moving average for four months but S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of such episodes.

mechanism_narrative: When FEDFUNDS is above 5% and CPIAUCSL is below 2% for three consecutive months, the economy is in a disinflationary high-rate regime, which typically coincides with positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days due to stabilized inflation expectations.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS > 5% and CPIAUCSL < 2% for three consecutive months
failure_condition: FEDFUNDS > 5% and CPIAUCSL < 2% for three months but S&P 500 60-day returns are negative in more than 60% of such regimes.
